packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-08 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my prior context revealed a proposed identification or earlier reading of this leaf. This is a blind reading. Note that the leaf itself is a list that names an owner and titles in its own words; I transcribe those words as written and add no identification of my own.

==== LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only) ====

image-001: overview of one face of a single leaf, upright, photographed on black with a wooden ruler (0-17 cm) below. image-002: native tile of the upper written area. image-003: native tile of the lower written area; its first two lines repeat the last two lines of image-002.

Observations
- Single column, long lines, written area only in the upper half; lower half blank. No running title, no rubric, no colour in the text. Edges of the leaf show traces of red (edge colouring); left edge ragged; a rectangular notch and a loss at the foot; an ink blot bottom right.
- A two-line heading: line 1 opens with a large calligraphic L with a tall looped ascender and is in a slightly larger script; line 2 is indented.
- Below the heading, ten list entries, each preceded in the left margin by a double slash "//". Second lines of long entries are indented without the slashes. A blank line (with a single dot at left) separates entries 5 and 6.
- Several entries end with a small tick/check-like stroke (after entries 1, 6, 7, 9; possibly a line-filler or a later check mark).
- In entry 4 the first two occurrences of the words "Cor ubi es" are underlined.
- Small superscript additions: a "v"-like mark above the first word of entry 1; superscript letters in abbreviations (4or, ven.lis, ven.le).
- Modern rectangular red ink stamp lower right: "ARCHIVUM / SEM. EPISC. / GANDAV."
- Cursive bookhand with heavy abbreviation; c and t are nearly indistinguishable, which affects several readings below.

Tentative interpretation: an ownership statement followed by a list of the contents of a volume (heading says the book "contains what follows"). The leaf would then be a flyleaf or contents leaf. I do not go beyond the wording on the leaf.

Areas selected: everything written on this face (2 heading lines, 10 entries). Unread: nothing substantial; the reverse is not shown. A view of the reverse would show whether the list continues.

Conventions: (..) = my expansion; ? = uncertain; [..] = unreadable. Line numbers count written lines from the top of each tile.

==== TRANSCRIPTION ====

Heading
image-002
 1  Liber fr(atru)m Regulariu(m) in s(an)c(t)o Leonardo iuxta leodiu(m) :
 2      Et (con)tinet(ur) in eo que sequu(n)t(ur) :

List (each "//" is the marginal double slash)
 3  // P(ri)mo 4or libri dyalogor(um) b(ea)ti g(re)gorij p(a)pe  [tick]
 4  // Rosacea? corona augustissi(m)e? cristifere? marie ·
 5  // Ep(isto)le et Carmi(n)a i(n) q(ui)b(us) repudiat(ur) filia regis ro(ma)nor(um)
 6      p(er) karolu(m) rege(m) fra(n)cor(um) viij?
 7  // Cor ubi es · i(n) deserto? · Cor ubi es i(n) tho(ro)? · Cor ubi es · i(n) dormito(ri)o
        (the first and second "Cor ubi es" are underlined; small raised "o" after "deserto?" and after "dormito")
 8  // Tabula i(n)dulge(n)ciar(um) ordi(ni)s cano(n)icor(um) regulariu(m) de wi(n)des(em)?

image-003 (lines 1-2 repeat image-002 lines 7-8)
    [blank line with a single dot at the left]
 3  // Tabulare fr(atru)m ordi(ni)s deifere v(ir)gi(ni)s ma(r)ie de carmelo  [tick]
 4  // Co(n)s(er)uatoriu(m) cleri ciuitatis (et) dioces(is) leodien(sis) p(er)petuu(m)  [tick]
 5  // Tractat(us) gerson de t(ri)bulat(i)o(n)ib(us) ex defectuoso regimi(n)e
 6      ecclesiasticor(um) adhuc eccl(esi)e p(ro)uenturis
 7  // Vita s(an)c(t)i Gerardi abb(at)is (et) co(n)fess(oris) fu(n)dato(r)is eccl(esi)e bronien(sis)  [tick]
 8  // Tractat(us) · de tractat(i)o(n)e (et) susceptio(n)e ven(erabi)lis sac(ra)m(en)ti in? sp(eci)e? (et)? g(e)n(er)ali
 9      2° de p(er)tine(n)tib(us) hoc ven(erabi)le sac(ra)m(entu)m · 3° de p(er)icul(is) (con)tinge(n)tib(us)
10      circa hoc ven(erabi)le sac(ra)m(entu)m :·

Notes on particular readings
- image-002 line 4: the first word could be read "Rosacea" or "Rosatea" (c/t ambiguity); the third word has a nasal bar and reads "augustissi(m)e" or "angustissi(m)e" (u/n ambiguity); the fourth word begins with c or t ("cristifere" / "tristifere"). I have not chosen by sense.
- image-002 line 6: the last element is minims plus a long j with a bar above; "viij" is my best reading, "iij" possible.
- image-002 line 7: the word after the first "i(n)" is "deserto" or "referto/reserto" (first letter unclear); the second place-word is "tho" with a suspension stroke.
- image-002 line 8: last word "wides" with abbreviation strokes; expansion uncertain.
- image-003 line 8: after "sac(ra)m(en)ti" there are two or three short abbreviated words before "g(e)n(er)ali" that I cannot resolve securely; a small ink spot sits on the "(et)" before "susceptio(n)e".
- "ven.lis" / "ven.le" carry the endings as superscript letters.

==== LIMITATIONS ====
- Heavy abbreviation; expansions in parentheses are mine and unverified.
- c/t and u/n ambiguity as noted; I have left alternatives visible.
- Only one face supplied; the reverse and any continuation are not seen.
- This is an unverified image reading.
